content:
Phase 67 implemented at afe6aee (branch phase/watcher-event-log-and-heartbeat, pushed). gate: see entry @ afe6aee — the one full-suite run is the gate's.

What / where
- tagteam/watchlog.py (new): Sink (event + beat writers under one threading.Lock), _open_regular (parent _dir_chain, leaf lstat refusal, O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK|O_CLOEXEC, fstat S_ISREG), rotation by os.replace at 512 KB with one .1, beat temp O_CREAT|O_EXCL with one unlink-and-retry, read / last_event / read_beat via safe_read.read_bounded, effective_every_s, beat_view, and the status/log command.
- tagteam/watcher.py: _log(msg, kind='info', **ctx) prints exactly as before and feeds _SINK when one is installed; _watch_locked installs the Sink and closes it in finally (independent of keep_pidfile; close removes only this pid's beat); body moved verbatim to _watch_sinked. 41 call sites tagged (positions taken from the AST, not regex); _beat(state) in the poll loop and the event loop's on_change; every_s set to 30 for the event loop and back to the interval on fallback; both 3.0-arc comments updated; watch_command dispatches status/log before its option loop.
- tagteam/cli.py: watch moves from READ_ONLY_REFUSED to READ_ONLY_COMMANDS as _sub_in('status','log'); help text.
- tagteam/cockpit_api.py + server.py: now.watcher gains beat (the beat_view dict) and last_event; GET /api/watcher/events?n= (clamped 1–500, junk n → 50).
- CLAUDE.md, README.md, roadmap, phase doc.

Approval notes: (1) staleness uses max(every_s, 5 s throttle) — test covers --interval 1 (9 s fresh, 16 s stale) and bad every_s values; (2) the leaf lstat refusal is kept ahead of the open and the docstring states what the guard is not.

Deviations — please check, all listed in the phase doc's 'Implementation notes':
1. in-turn is wider than the plan: the loop also blocks inside gate runs (minutes), panels and briefs, which claim the slot with watcher_pid = the watcher. Implemented rule: the in-flight record's runner IS the beat's watcher (pid equal, ident not contradicting). Conversations (server pid), other/earlier watchers and dead runners still do not exempt; a gate marker has pid None so child-pid liveness is not required.
2. 'slot-busy' dropped from KINDS: that line comes from the headless engine through its log= callable; tagging it means changing the engine's logging signature, which the plan excluded. 18 kinds, pinned against the source by test.
3. docs/workflows.md untouched: it lists modes not commands, and it is a managed file — two lines would refresh it in every registered project.
4. watch status truncates the last-dispatch message to 100 chars; watch log never does.

Verified
- tests/test_watchlog.py: 56 tests — exact kind sequence from a scripted processor run with context; no-sink byte-identical print; FIFO/symlink at event path, .1, beat path, beat temp name and .tagteam itself (under SIGALRM, link targets byte-identical); lstat-then-FIFO swap; OSError on open/write/replace swallowed; dispatch proceeds with an unwritable log; rotation + read across generations; 8-thread writers across rotation (whole lines, per-thread unbroken tails); throttled and concurrent beats; sink install/removal with pidfile False and True; beat_view table; CLI under TAGTEAM_READ_ONLY writes nothing and every other watch invocation is still refused through the real CLI; API payloads and the tokenless GET.
- Focused run of the ten touched/adjacent files: 393 passed, 2 skipped.
- Real process, scratch project: tagteam watch --mode notify --poll --interval 2 → watch status showed running/pid, 'last look: 2s ago', the refused dispatch; after SIGTERM the beat was removed, the log ended with kind stop and matched the process stdout line for line.
- NOT verified: criterion 10 on this repo. The iTerm2 watcher running here predates the change and holds the old code, so it records nothing until the arbiter restarts that tab.

Gate bounce r1 addressed at 8eaf7b1. gate: see entry @ 8eaf7b1.

The r1 gate run was 2,197 passed / 1 failed: tests/test_headless.py::TestWatcherIntegration::test_build_processor_headless_paused_marker_logged replaces watcher._log with logs.append, which cannot take the new kind=/context keywords (TypeError from _log_startup_banner's kind='start'). A real consequence of the signature change, not a flake. Fix is test-side only: the two stand-ins for watcher._log in the suite (tests/test_headless.py:956, tests/test_briefer.py:163 — the second passed only because its path logs no tagged line) now accept **_kw. No product code changed since afe6aee. This does amend the plan's 'existing watcher tests pass unchanged': two tests that swap out a private function needed the new signature; every test that calls the watcher rather than replacing _log passed unchanged.

Focused: test_headless TestWatcherIntegration + test_briefer + test_watchlog = 107 passed. Everything else in the round-1 submission stands (what/where, the four listed deviations, what was and was not verified — criterion 10 on this repo still needs the arbiter to restart the iTerm2 watcher tab).

Gate bounce r2 addressed at HEAD (test-only). gate: see entry @ this commit.

r2 gate run: 2,197 passed / 1 failed — tests/test_watcher_lock.py::test_start_watcher_reports_refusal_as_already_running, the issue-10 flake. The r1 failure (the _log stand-in) was fixed and did not recur. This time Phase 65's _child_output made the flake explain itself: the spawned watcher had exited 1 with 'refused: another watcher is already running for this project (pid <pytest pid>, probe, …)'. Cause: the test waited with _lock_free(), which ACQUIRES the exclusive lock as mode 'probe' every 0.1 s (holding it across the ps call in procs.identity); the child's single non-blocking attempt landed inside a probe and was refused. Reproduced deterministically outside pytest: hold the lock as 'probe', run tagteam watch → exit 1 with that exact message naming the holder's pid. Not a product defect (a second watcher should be refused while the lock is held) and not caused by Phase 67, though this phase adds a procs.identity call at watcher start-up, which shifts the timing.

Fix, tests only: that one wait now uses _lock_held_by(root, pid), which reads the lock's record and takes no lock; the other six _lock_free uses run when nothing is racing and are unchanged. tests/test_watcher_lock.py: 20 passed, six consecutive runs (24–28 s each) — consistent with the fix, not proof of a rate. Issue 10 in docs/tagteam-issues-release-and-venv-upgrade-2026-09-20.md now records the cause. This is outside the Phase 67 plan's file list; included because it blocks the gate and the evidence arrived here. No product code changed since afe6aee; everything in the round-1 submission stands, including the four listed deviations and the unverified criterion 10 on this repo.

GATE: PASS | scope 12 paths | plan-doc ok | tests ok (2198 passed, 5 skipped, 7m47s)
checked: HEAD 1cbeb37

Reviewed implementation through 1cbeb37 against the approved plan. Two reproducible correctness gaps need fixes:

1. tagteam/watchlog.py:256-262: last_event silently scans only 400 records. A retained dispatch disappears from both watch status and now.watcher.last_event after 400 info lines, even though the bounded files still contain it. Reproduced in a temporary project: write one sent event and 401 info events; read(root, 1000) returns all 402, but both last_event(root) and last_event(root, DISPATCH_KINDS) return None. Search the bounded retained generations for the newest matching event (live first, then .1), rather than an arbitrary record-count suffix. Add regression coverage for more than 400 chatter records and a match in .1. This preserves the existing byte bound while honoring 'newest non-info / last dispatch'.

2. tagteam/watcher.py:1844-1853: clean event-driven shutdown records no stop. watcher_events.watch_with_events catches KeyboardInterrupt internally, stops/joins its observer, then returns normally; the outer except KeyboardInterrupt does not execute on that normal shutdown path. Reproduced by modeling that normal return: _run_event_loop returns True with zero stop records. Record exactly one stop on clean normal return as well as the propagated-interrupt path; keep error/fallback distinct. Add an event-mode shutdown regression modeling the inner handler (poll-only coverage currently passes).

Accepted deviations: the broader in-turn exemption based on matching watcher owner is supported by the synchronous gate/panel/briefer slot records (gate has no child pid); dropping slot-busy avoids expanding the engine logging signature; status truncation and leaving the managed workflows file unchanged are reasonable. The _log test stand-in updates are required by the new private signature. The watcher-lock test change is justified by the captured 'probe' refusal: its old readiness probe competed for the same lock, and the new read-only record check removes that cause.

Verification: gate PASS @ 1cbeb37: 2198 passed, 5 skipped; accepted without rerunning the suite. Reviewer focused tests/test_watchlog.py: 56 passed. git diff --check dcf4f2e..HEAD clean. Both reproductions used temporary projects, with no product edits. The submitted scratch-process smoke is useful; the real iTerm2 handoff check remains explicitly unverified and must not be marked complete in closeout without evidence.
